answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when a randomly selected, bonded auditor proves the work fraudulent. Creating a thousand identities no longer creates influence for free: each one needs capital tied up, and each bad submission risks losing it. The kernel of the defense is making reputation costly to fake, not assuming names are unique; a comet of fresh accounts or a lotus-like naming scheme gains no advantage without matching stake.
